security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline table formatting, and placeholder Azure endpoint examples. No prompt injection, credential theft, hidden command execution, or unauthorized data exfiltration intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Placeholder Application Insights endpoints may be mistaken for hardcoded destinations.
remediation.suggestion: State that users must provide their own Application Insights connection string or Azure credential, and avoid embedding real instrumentation keys.

content.user_title: Configure Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry for Python
content.value_statement: Python teams need reliable observability without complex setup across web frameworks and background services. This skill provides focused Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry guidance for traces, metrics, logs, sampling, and Application Insights configuration.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install the Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry Python package.
Explains environment variable and explicit connection string setup for Application Insights.
Provides setup examples for Flask, Django, and FastAPI applications.
Demonstrates custom traces, metrics, and Python logging integration.
Covers sampling, cloud role names, selected instrumentation, live metrics, and Azure AD authentication.
limitations: It does not validate Azure credentials, connection strings, or subscription permissions.
It does not deploy Azure Monitor resources or create Application Insights instances.
It does not tune telemetry volume for a specific production workload.
It does not replace privacy review for logs, traces, or custom attributes.

use_cases.title: Add Observability to a Python Web App
use_cases.description: Configure Application Insights collection for Flask, Django, or FastAPI with minimal code changes.

use_cases.title: Standardize Azure Telemetry Setup
use_cases.description: Create consistent tracing, metrics, logging, and sampling guidance across Python services.

use_cases.title: Review Production Telemetry Configuration
use_cases.description: Check service names, authentication choices, instrumentation scope, and sampling settings before release.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Setup
prompt_templates.scenario: Start a new Application Insights integration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me the minimal steps to configure Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry for a Python application using an environment variable.

prompt_templates.title: Framework Integration
prompt_templates.scenario: Apply the setup to a web framework.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me add Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry to my FastAPI service and explain where configure_azure_monitor should be called.

prompt_templates.title: Telemetry Customization
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a Python telemetry setup that includes custom spans, custom metrics, structured logs, sampling, and a cloud role name.

prompt_templates.title: Production Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate an existing service before deployment.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry plan for a production Django service, including authentication, sampling, instrumentations, and privacy risks.

output_examples.input: Set up Application Insights for a small Flask service.
output_examples.output: A short implementation plan with package installation, connection string placement, early configuration, Flask startup order, and validation steps in Azure Portal.

output_examples.input: Add useful telemetry to a background worker.
output_examples.output: Recommendations for custom spans around work units, counters for processed jobs, structured error logs, sampling choices, and service naming.
A checklist covering credential strategy, environment variables, telemetry volume, sensitive data handling, live metrics, and dashboard validation.

best_practices: Call Azure Monitor configuration before importing libraries that should be auto-instrumented.
Use environment variables or Azure AD authentication instead of embedding real connection strings in code.
Review logs, span attributes, and custom metrics for sensitive data before production use.
anti_patterns: Do not paste real instrumentation keys into source files, examples, tickets, or prompts.
Do not enable full telemetry volume in high-traffic services without a sampling decision.
Do not assume auto-instrumentation covers every custom operation without adding spans or metrics.

faq.question: What does this skill help me configure?
faq.answer: It helps configure Azure Monitor OpenTelemetry for Python applications that send telemetry to Application Insights.

faq.question: Does it create Azure resources?
faq.answer: No. It explains application-side setup and assumes the required Azure resources already exist.

faq.question: Which Python frameworks are covered?
faq.answer: The examples cover Flask, Django, and FastAPI, plus generic traces, metrics, and logs.

faq.question: Can I use Azure AD authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill includes guidance for using DefaultAzureCredential with Azure Monitor configuration.

faq.question: Does the skill handle sensitive telemetry data?
faq.answer: It does not inspect data. Users must review logs, attributes, and traces before sending telemetry.

faq.question: Is this only for Claude?
faq.answer: No. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
